interpretive_notes.title: Keep the Hydro operating lineage distinct from the 1964 corporation
interpretive_notes.assessment: The 30 March 1962 original commencement is well supported, and the 20 August 1965 ends of BC Electric and the Power Commission are well supported by the agreement ratified in the 1966 Act. It is reasonable to keep one public-facing Hydro lineage if the dates are typed. A continuous lineage from 1962 is not a finding that the modern legal corporation was constituted in 1962. R4E-C035 identifies its new 1964 constitution, effective 23 March 1964. The event for the 1963 judgment already correctly preserves contemporary annual-report attribution and the fact that the judgment and any appellate outcome were not recovered.
interpretive_notes.recommended_wording: BC Hydro’s operating lineage begins under the 1962 scheme on 30 March 1962. Following the judicial invalidity reported in Hydro’s contemporary annual report, a new corporation was constituted under the 1964 Act on 23 March 1964. BC Electric and the Power Commission ceased separate corporate existence under the amalgamation effective 20 August 1965.
interpretive_notes.avoid: Do not summarize the whole display as the settled legal identity from 1962, or imply the full 1963 judgment was inspected. Do not undo the 1965 ends merely because the full judgment is unavailable: the later ratified agreement directly establishes those ends.

interpretive_notes.title: Harbours transfer provisions should retain their conditions and relationship type
interpretive_notes.assessment: Dissolution on 30 May 1985 is secure. The 1983 Act authorizes specified asset/liability transfers to BC Development Corporation and BC Railway on separately fixed transfer dates. R4E-C046 expressly leaves those orders/dates unresolved. The body text converts this into a completed division of assets, and serviceSuccessorIds makes the relation a service lineage. The cited Public Accounts independently proves a railway-asset exchange in fiscal 1983/84, but that does not supply every executed transfer or convert all asset transfers into service succession.
interpretive_notes.correction: State that the Act provided for the transfers; record separately the railway-asset exchange reported for the year ended 31 March 1984. Use asset-transfer relationships until service succession is independently established. Recover the actual transfer orders for complete dated edges.

claim_evidence.subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited and British Columbia Power Commission
claim_evidence.claim: The agreement reproduced in the Power Measures Act 1966 takes effect at 5 p.m. local Vancouver time on 20 August 1965. The three bodies continue as the Hydro authority established under the 1964 Act, and BC Electric and the Power Commission cease separate corporate existence.
claim_evidence.locator: 1966 Act s3 and Schedule clauses 1–2, printed pp241–242
claim_evidence.caveat: The ratifying Act assented on 1 April 1966 expressly validates the 20 August 1965 agreement. Do not date the amalgamation to the later assent.
claim_evidence.successor: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority established by the 1964 Act

claim_evidence.subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim_evidence.claim: OIC 2387/1965 separately revokes and cancels BC Electric’s incorporation and declares it dissolved after reciting that the amalgamation had already occurred.
claim_evidence.caveat: This is the later formal corporate cancellation/dissolution event; the agreement says separate existence ceased on 20 August.

claim_evidence.subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim_evidence.claim: Power Measures Act 1966 section 5 deems the Crown-held BC Electric common shares surrendered to Hydro and cancelled immediately upon the amalgamation.
claim_evidence.caveat: Statutory retroactive confirmation, assented to 1 April 1966.

claim_evidence.subject: British Columbia Harbours Board
claim_evidence.claim: Sections 2 and 3 of the Harbour Board Repeal Act commenced under OIC 1061/1985 on 30 May 1985, repealing the Harbour Board Act, dissolving the board and terminating members’ appointments. The date is expressly confirmed in Public Accounts.
claim_evidence.locator: 1983 Act ss2,3,8; OIC 1061; Public Accounts 1984/85 C24 note 19(b)
claim_evidence.caveat: The repeal Act assented on 23 September 1983; that is not the board’s dissolution date. Sections 4–5 authorize transfers to BC Development Corporation and BC Railway Company, but their precise transfer orders/dates are not supplied by OIC 1061.

findings.title: Unknown ends cannot be represented without indefinite presence
findings.finding: Null end means indefinite existence; historical search also excludes null-ended records. A status-only fix would leave navigation, timeline and panel misleading.

findings.title: Subsidiary relation becomes accountability path
findings.finding: Powertech parents have relation subsidiary_of; snapshot emits part, which pathToPeople traverses. Direct 2026 probe returns a complete uninferred path through BC Hydro.
findings.recommendation: Preserve subsidiary_of/owned_by and exclude it from accountability traversal. Require a distinct sourced responsibility edge. Use separate board-appointment type from the traversable appoints edge.

findings.title: Local-register description overstates uniform non-operation and elected trustees
findings.finding: The blanket statement that neither district type runs a hospital is too strong. Original Fort Nelson and 100 Mile House instruments assign hospital board-of-management roles to the district trustees plus a Hospital Act appointee. Fort Nelson's first trustees were appointed, with later elections.
findings.recommendation: State body-specific functions and dated governance. Financial-assistance objects alone do not prove hospital operation; hospital-management clauses must not be erased. Do not infer the legal hospital operator solely from shared trustees.

findings.title: A register excluded from all diagram consumption does not complete local history
findings.finding: Separate local identities are correct, but the proposal explicitly makes the register unread by the diagram build. No-ministry status is not no local democratic accountability.
findings.recommendation: Read local records into shared identity/search/event/panel resolvers. Add optional local/regional layer with own governance and electorate profiles; do not force ministerial parenting. Replace no-ministry-only explanation for local records.

findings.title: Recommendation-only minister role discards precise statutory relationships
findings.finding: The proposal forbids minister roles beyond recommendation despite held evidence for capital approval and inspection powers.
findings.recommendation: Keep approvals, inspection and appointments as typed, dated relationships without converting them to responsibility. Preserve the 2026 current-law checkpoint as an observation rather than backdating it.

findings.title: Date precision and end-event meaning are collapsed

legal_chain: Section 8 of the 2002 Act repeals the Forest Renewal Act.

Section 28(1) dissolves Forest Renewal BC and its section 5 committees upon that repeal, rescinds board/committee appointments, vests rights/property/assets in government and makes government liable for obligations.
Section 32 postpones relevant provisions to LGIC regulation.

Regulation 158/2002 was deposited 27 June 2002; the Regulations Act default deposit rule fixes that effective date.
